title: Emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces in hybrid Al/InAs heterostructures
authors: S. Feyrer, V. Dimic, I. Lobato, A. Kirchner, P. Drexler, L. Rupp, D. Bougeard, T. Lindemann, S. Gronin, G. Gardner, M. J. Manfra, G. F. R. Ruiz, C. A. Balseiro, L. Arrachea, M. Aprili, N. Paradiso, C. Strunk, L. Tosi
abstract: We investigate the microwave electrodynamics of a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures. Using lumped-element resonators with inductor wires oriented relative to an in-plane magnetic field, we directly probe the superfluid stiffness via the kinetic inductance. As the field increases, the resonance frequency exhibits a non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution that cannot be explained by orbital pair breaking alone. We show that this behavior is consistent with the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces, which selectively suppress the supercurrent response depending on the direction of the magnetic field. Microscopic calculations of the stiffness tensor capture the observed anisotropy driven by the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects. Our results establish microwave stiffness measurements as a sensitive probe of anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid systems.
summary: The paper reports on experimental and theoretical investigations into superconductivity in Al/InAs hybrid structures. By measuring the microwave electrodynamics, the authors detect an anisotropic suppression of superfluid stiffness that signals the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces. This work establishes microwave measurements as a sensitive tool for probing gapless superconducting phases.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of Bogoliubov Fermi Surfaces (BFS) and characterizes anisotropic gapless superconductivity in hybrid superconductor/semiconductor heterostructures.
main_result: The observed non-monotonic and strongly anisotropic evolution of the superfluid stiffness, measured via microwave electrodynamics, is consistent with the formation of BFS due to the interplay of Zeeman and orbital Fulde-Ferrell effects.
method: The research combines microwave electrodynamic measurements (probing kinetic inductance) with microscopic theoretical calculations based on the Bogoliubov-de Gennes framework.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid Al/InAs heterostructure containing a 2DEG proximitized by an Al superconductor. The theory models the superconducting response using the superfluid stiffness tensor derived from the free energy density.
key_observables: Superfluid stiffness tensor components ($D_{ij}$), relative frequency shift ($\Delta f_0 / f_0$), and internal quality factor change ($Q_i$) as functions of in-plane magnetic field and angle.
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field ($B$), Zeeman energy ($V_Z$), Doppler energy ($V_D$), superconducting gap ($\Delta_0$), and temperature ($T$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the electrodynamic response can be mapped to the superfluid stiffness tensor, and theoretical models rely on specific approximations regarding disorder effects and gauge equivalence.
figures_summary: Figures show sample setups, microwave resonance curves demonstrating field dependence, theoretical band structure evolution illustrating gap closing and BFS formation, and quantitative maps detailing angular anisotropy of stiffness suppression.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from experimental characterization using microwave resonators to establishing the link between anisotropic response and BFS emergence. It then uses microscopic theory (BdG) to model this behavior, followed by fitting measured superfluid density data to confirm the theoretical predictions regarding field-induced gapless phases.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete platform for observing exotic superconducting states predicted in proximity systems, linking macroscopic transport measurements (microwave response) directly to microscopic band structure features like BFS.
